'''''All the Money in the World''''' is a 2017 biographical [[crime thriller film]] directed by [[Ridley Scott]] and written by [[David Scarpa]]. Based on [[John Pearson (author)|John Pearson]]'s 1995 book ''Painfully Rich: The Outrageous Fortunes and Misfortunes of the Heirs of J. Paul Getty'', it depicts the events surrounding the 1973 kidnapping of [[John Paul Getty III]] and the refusal of his grandfather, the multi-billionaire oil tycoon [[J. Paul Getty]], to cooperate with the kidnappers' extortion demands. The film stars [[Michelle Williams (actress)|Michelle Williams]] as Gail Harris Getty, John Paul Getty III's mother; [[Christopher Plummer]] as J. Paul Getty; and [[Mark Wahlberg]] as Fletcher Chace, an adviser of the Getty family.

Principal photography began in March 2017 and was completed in August for a December 8 release. Two months before the scheduled premiere, sexual misconduct allegations were made against J. Paul Getty's original actor [[Kevin Spacey]], leading to his removal from the film.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Cranswick|first1=Amie|title=First poster and trailer for Ridley Scott's All the Money in the World|url=https://www.flickeringmyth.com/2017/09/first-poster-and-trailer-for-ridley-scotts-all-the-money-in-the-world/|website=FlickeringMyth.com|publisher=Flickering Myth|access-date=December 12, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180828030638/https://www.flickeringmyth.com/2017/09/first-poster-and-trailer-for-ridley-scotts-all-the-money-in-the-world/|archive-date=August 28, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> Plummer was cast by November and 22 scenes were reshot within eight days, one month prior to the rescheduled Christmas release date.<ref name=PlummerRecast>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2017/11/kevin-spacey-dropped-all-in-the-money-in-the-world-christopher-plummer-ridley-scott-j-paul-getty-1202204437/|title=Shocker: Kevin Spacey Dropped From 'All The Money In The World;' J Paul Getty Role Recast With Christopher Plummer|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=November 8, 2017|access-date=November 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171109020204/http://deadline.com/2017/11/kevin-spacey-dropped-all-in-the-money-in-the-world-christopher-plummer-ridley-scott-j-paul-getty-1202204437/|archive-date=November 9, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|last1=Kreps|first1=Daniel|title=See Christopher Plummer Replace Kevin Spacey in New 'All the Money in the World' Spot|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/news/see-christopher-plummer-replace-kevin-spacey-in-new-film-spot-w512807|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|access-date=December 21, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222053227/https://www.rollingstone.com/movies/news/see-christopher-plummer-replace-kevin-spacey-in-new-film-spot-w512807|archive-date=December 22, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> It was later reported that Wahlberg was paid $1.5&nbsp;million for the reshoots, while Williams was only paid $1,000, which sparked a debate on the [[gender pay gap]] in Hollywood.

The film premiered at the [[Samuel Goldwyn Theater]] in [[Beverly Hills]] on December 18, 2017, followed by a United States theatrical release by [[TriStar Pictures]] on December 25. It received generally favorable reviews, many of which praised the performances, and grossed only $57&nbsp;million against a $50&nbsp;million budget. Plummer received particular acclaim, and he was nominated for the [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] for [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor|Best Supporting Actor]] for his work in the film.

==Plot==
In 1973, 16-year-old [[John Paul Getty III]], grandson of the world's richest private citizen, oil tycoon [[J. Paul Getty]], is kidnapped in [[Rome]], where he lives, by the [['Ndrangheta]], a [[Mafia]]-like [[organized crime]] group based in [[Calabria]]. A ransom of $17&nbsp;million is demanded, but Paul's mother, Gail Harris Getty, is unable to pay it, as she rejected any alimony in exchange for full custody of her children when she divorced Paul's father, [[John Paul Getty Jr.]], in 1971{{efn|In reality, Abigail Harris and John Paul Getty Jr. were divorced in 1964.}} due to his [[drug addiction]]. She travels to Getty's [[Sutton Place, Surrey|estate in England]] to beseech him to provide the money, but he refuses, stating that doing so would encourage further kidnappings of his family members, and instead asks Fletcher Chace, a [[Getty Oil]] negotiator and former [[CIA]] operative, to investigate the case and secure Paul's release. The media quickly picks up on the story, and Gail is constantly hounded by [[paparazzi]].

Paul is kept hostage in a remote location in southern Italy. Initially, his captors, particularly Cinquanta, do not treat him overly harshly, as he causes them few problems, but as months go by without the ransom being paid, far longer than the captors anticipated, the situation grows increasingly tense. One of the kidnappers accidentally shows his face to Paul, but, before he can kill Paul so he cannot be identified, another kidnapper shoots him dead. His burned and disfigured body is found in the sea, and, at first, investigators think it is Paul. Gail is brought in to identify her son, but immediately sees that the corpse is not him.

Once they determine the correct identity of the body, the [[Carabinieri]] are able to determine where Paul is being held. A raid is conducted, during the course of which all of the kidnappers who are present are killed, but Paul is not found, as he has been sold to a different [['ndrina]], or crime family, who hire Cinquanta to keep looking after Paul and negotiating with Gail. Paul's new captors are much less patient, and more ruthless, than his former ones, and, after he almost escapes, they cut off one of his ears and mail it to a newspaper, claiming they will continue mutilating the boy until the ransom is paid.

After repeated negotiations between the captors and Gail and Chace, the ransom is lowered to $4&nbsp;million. Getty finally agrees to pay, but only if Gail signs over full custody of all of her children to their father, who is in a near-[[Persistent vegetative state|vegetative state]] due to his drug use. Knowing she is really giving custody to Getty, Gail signs the documents, but Getty only provides $1&nbsp;million, as it is the maximum amount his lawyers can figure out a way to claim as tax-deductible. Gail announces she has the full ransom, hoping she and Chace can figure out a way to get Paul back alive anyway, and the desperation of this, coupled with a biting resignation speech given by Chace, unintentionally convince Getty to provide the full ransom and give Gail back the custody of her children.

Following precise instructions from the captors, Gail and Chace leave the money in a remote location and, once it is counted, receive a call to pick up Paul from a construction site. Based on advice from Cinquanta, Paul has run away, so Gail and Chace begin to search for him. The captors also begin to search for Paul, intending to kill him, after they discover Chace broke his word by leading the police to them. Everyone converges on the nearby town of [[Lauria]] after dark, and some of the criminals are arrested, but one of them finds Paul. Cinquanta attacks the man to allow Paul to escape, and Paul is reunited with Gail and brought to safety.

When Getty dies in 1976, Gail is tasked with managing her children's inherited wealth until they are adults. Getty's estate was set up as a [[charitable trust]], which allowed him to avoid paying taxes, but also meant he could not spend his income. He could invest it, however, and amassed an enormous collection of paintings, sculptures, and other artifacts, most of which now reside in the [[J. Paul Getty Museum]] in Los Angeles.

==Production==
===Development and pre-production===
[[File:NASA Journey to Mars and “The Martian” (201508180030HQ).jpg|thumb|Director Scott in 2015]]
On March 13, 2017, it was reported that [[Ridley Scott]] was finalizing plans to direct the [[David Scarpa]]-scripted ''All the Money in the World'', a film about the kidnapping of [[John Paul Getty III]]. Scott stated he was attracted to the project because of Scarpa's script, adding: "I just consumed it [...] I knew about the kidnapping, but this story was very, very provocative... Gail Getty was an exceptional character, and there are many facets of the man Getty that make him a really great study. There's this great dynamic. It was like a play, and not a movie."<ref name="auto">{{cite magazine|url=https://ew.com/movies/2017/08/11/all-the-money-in-the-world-ridley-scott-kevin-spacey-michelle-williams/|last=Li|first=Shirley|title=Ridley Scott talks casting Kevin Spacey, Michelle Williams in Getty kidnapping thriller|date=August 11, 2017|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|access-date=September 20, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170921001246/http://ew.com/movies/2017/08/11/all-the-money-in-the-world-ridley-scott-kevin-spacey-michelle-williams/|archive-date=September 21, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Natalie Portman]] was pursued for the role of Gail Harris at one point,<ref>{{cite news|last1=Fleming|first1=Mike Jr.|title=Ridley Scott To Next Helm Getty Kidnap Drama; Natalie Portman Courted|url=https://deadline.com/2017/03/ridley-scott-j-paul-getty-iii-kidnap-movie-natalie-portman-david-scarpa-john-paul-getty-1202042231/|date=March 13, 2017|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=June 14, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170609090149/http://deadline.com/2017/03/ridley-scott-j-paul-getty-iii-kidnap-movie-natalie-portman-david-scarpa-john-paul-getty-1202042231/|archive-date=June 9, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> but, on March 31, 2017, it was reported that [[Michelle Williams (actress)|Michelle Williams]] and [[Kevin Spacey]] were circling the roles of Harris and [[J. Paul Getty]], respectively, while [[Mark Wahlberg]] was in talks for an unspecified role.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Fleming|first1=Mike Jr.|title=Michelle Williams, Kevin Spacey, Mark Wahlberg Circling Ridley Scott's Getty Kidnap Film|url=https://deadline.com/2017/03/michelle-williams-kevin-spacey-mark-wahlberg-ridley-scott-getty-kidnap-film-imperative-entertainment-sony-pictures-1202056971/|date=March 31, 2017|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=June 14, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170609082300/http://deadline.com/2017/03/michelle-williams-kevin-spacey-mark-wahlberg-ridley-scott-getty-kidnap-film-imperative-entertainment-sony-pictures-1202056971/|archive-date=June 9, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> On casting Spacey, Scott stated: "When I read the script, I started thinking, 'Who was Paul Getty?' In my mind, I saw Kevin Spacey. Kevin's a brilliant actor, but I've never worked with him, and I always knew I would have to have him portray Getty in this film [...] He was so obsessed with what he was doing [...] He wasn't giving people a second thought." Regarding Williams, Scott stated that, while she was not his first choice, "Michelle is very special as an actress, and I've never done anything with her before [...] The family was very private and there was very little footage of [Gail], but around the kidnapping, there was one particular interview she did that Michelle jumped at, and it shows Gail Getty being very assertive, very smart," both qualities Williams possessed.<ref name="auto"/> [[Charlie Plummer]] joined the cast as John Paul Getty III on May 2,<ref>{{cite news|last1=Kroll|first1=Justin|title=Ridley Scott's Getty Drama Casts Charlie Plummer as Kidnapped Grandson (EXCLUSIVE)|url=https://variety.com/2017/film/news/ridley-scott-getty-kidnapping-movie-grandson-charlie-plummer-1202405945/|date=May 2, 2017|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date=June 14, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171223102323/https://variety.com/2017/film/news/ridley-scott-getty-kidnapping-movie-grandson-charlie-plummer-1202405945/|archive-date=December 23, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> and [[Timothy Hutton]] was cast on June 16.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://deadline.com/2017/06/timothy-hutton-getty-kidnap-ridley-scott-all-the-money-in-the-world-1202115002/|title=Timothy Hutton Joins Ridley Scott's Getty Kidnap Thriller 'All The Money In The World'|last=Fleming|first=Mike Jr.|date=June 16, 2017|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=June 17, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170619042027/http://deadline.com/2017/06/timothy-hutton-getty-kidnap-ridley-scott-all-the-money-in-the-world-1202115002/|archive-date=June 19, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Initial filming===
It was reported on May 31, 2017, that the film had already begun [[principal photography]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=D'Alessandro|first1=Anthony|title=Michelle Williams Joins Amy Schumer In 'I Feel Pretty'|url=https://deadline.com/2017/05/michelle-williams-joins-amy-schumer-in-i-feel-pretty-1202105494/|date=May 31, 2017|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=June 14, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170904154843/http://deadline.com/2017/05/michelle-williams-joins-amy-schumer-in-i-feel-pretty-1202105494/|archive-date=September 4, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> At the end of July, a week of filming took place at [[Elveden Hall]] in [[Suffolk]], with the aristocratic, Grade II-listed stately home doubling as a Moroccan palace in a series of flashback scenes.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.eadt.co.uk/what-s-on/ridley-scott-brings-latest-blockbuster-all-the-money-in-the-world-to-film-in-suffolk-1-5183811|title=Ridley Scott brings latest blockbuster All the Money in the World to film in Suffolk – What's on and things to do in Suffolk|last=Noble|first=Jason|date=September 7, 2017|work=East Anglian Daily Times|access-date=September 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171204120552/http://www.eadt.co.uk/what-s-on/ridley-scott-brings-latest-blockbuster-all-the-money-in-the-world-to-film-in-suffolk-1-5183811|archive-date=December 4, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> Production reportedly concluded in August.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://variety.com/2017/film/in-contention/oscars-clint-eastwood-steven-spielberg-ridley-scott-1202532168/ |title=Oscars: Clint Eastwood, Steven Spielberg, Ridley Scott Race to the Finish |last=Tapley |first=Kristopher |date=August 18, 2017 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |access-date=December 14, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171213023004/http://variety.com/2017/film/in-contention/oscars-clint-eastwood-steven-spielberg-ridley-scott-1202532168/ |archive-date=December 13, 2017 |url-status=live }}</ref>

2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200108143056/https://collider.com/all-the-money-in-the-world-tv-spot-christopher-plummer/|archive-date=January 8, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://variety.com/2017/film/news/all-the-money-in-the-world-trailer-christopher-plummer-kevin-spacey-1202626065/|title='All the Money in the World' New Trailer Shows Christopher Plummer in Kevin Spacey's Previous Role|last=McNary|first=Dave|date=November 29, 2017|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date=December 14, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171215060412/http://variety.com/2017/film/news/all-the-money-in-the-world-trailer-christopher-plummer-kevin-spacey-1202626065/|archive-date=December 15, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> The only shot in the finished film that features Spacey is a wide shot of Getty disembarking from a train in the desert, as it would have been too expensive or complex to reshoot before the deadline, but Spacey's face is not visible.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=http://www.businessinsider.com/kevin-spacey-shot-all-the-money-in-the-world-christopher-plummer-ridley-scott-2017-12|title=Christopher Plummer replaced Kevin Spacey in 'All the Money in the World' — but there's one shot where you can still see Spacey|work=[[Business Insider]]|access-date=January 9, 2018|date=December 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180108120429/http://www.businessinsider.com/kevin-spacey-shot-all-the-money-in-the-world-christopher-plummer-ridley-scott-2017-12|archive-date=January 8, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> The reshoots cost $10&nbsp;million, bringing the film's final production budget to $50&nbsp;million.<ref name="re">{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/all-money-world-triggers-wage-gap-debate-1074207|title='All The Money in The World' Triggers Wage Gap Debate|author=Gregg Kilday|date=January 11, 2018|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|access-date=January 12, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180112051811/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/all-money-world-triggers-wage-gap-debate-1074207|archive-date=January 12, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2017/film/news/kevin-spacey-christopher-plummer-all-the-money-in-the-world-1202611975/|title=Replacing Kevin Spacey on 'All the Money in the World' Will Cost Millions|last1=Lang|first1=Brent|last2=Kroll|first2=Justin|date=November 10, 2017|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date=November 13, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171111014835/http://variety.com/2017/film/news/kevin-spacey-christopher-plummer-all-the-money-in-the-world-1202611975/|archive-date=November 11, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>

While it was initially reported that the actors filmed the reshoots for free,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/movies/2017/12/19/michelle-williams-mark-wahlberg-reshot-kevin-spaceys-all-money-scenes-free/966670001/|title=Michelle Williams, Mark Wahlberg reshot Kevin Spacey's 'All the Money' scenes for free|last=Mandell|first=Andrea|date=December 19, 2017|work=[[USA Today]]|access-date=December 30, 2017|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180101043949/https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/movies/2017/12/19/michelle-williams-mark-wahlberg-reshot-kevin-spaceys-all-money-scenes-free/966670001/|archive-date=January 1, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> it was later revealed that Wahlberg had been paid $1.5&nbsp;million, while Williams received only $80 in [[per diem]]s. Wahlberg's fee for the original shooting was allegedly $5&nbsp;million, whereas Williams' fee was allegedly $625,000.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/sharing-salaries-how-actresses-are-fighting-hollywoods-gender-pay-disparity-transparency-1075132 |title=Sharing Salaries: How Actresses Are Fighting Hollywood's Gender Pay Disparity With Transparency |work=The Hollywood Reporter |last=Siegel |first=Tatiana |date=January 18, 2018 |access-date=January 19, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180119034038/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/sharing-salaries-how-actresses-are-fighting-hollywoods-gender-pay-disparity-transparency-1075132 |archive-date=January 19, 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[The New York Times]]'' reported that Wahlberg accepted 80 percent less than his usual fee to work on this film, and the $1.5&nbsp;million he received for the reshoots was in addition to this. ''[[USA Today]]'' reported that Wahlberg was able to command the additional fee by refusing to agree to Plummer's casting until he was guaranteed the extra pay, as there was a clause in his contract that gave him approval of his co-stars.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/people/2018/01/11/exclusive-mark-wahlberg-refused-approve-christopher-plummer-unless-he-paid/1026347001/ |title=Exclusive: Mark Wahlberg refused to approve Christopher Plummer unless he was paid |work=[[USA Today]] |first=Andrea |last=Mandell |date=January 11, 2018 |access-date=January 12, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180112005735/https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/people/2018/01/11/exclusive-mark-wahlberg-refused-approve-christopher-plummer-unless-he-paid/1026347001/ |archive-date=January 12, 2018 |url-status=live }}</ref> As a result of the backlash brought on by the disparity in the actors' pay, Wahlberg announced he would donate the $1.5&nbsp;million to the [[Time's Up Legal Defense Fund]] in Williams' name.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/mark-wahlberg-donates-his-fee-all-money-reshoots-1074565|title=Mark Wahlberg and Agency Give $2M to Time's Up Fund After Pay Discrepancy Outcry|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|first=Andrea|last=Mandell|date=January 13, 2018|access-date=January 13, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113180552/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/mark-wahlberg-donates-his-fee-all-money-reshoots-1074565|archive-date=January 13, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Release==
The film premiered at the [[Samuel Goldwyn Theater]] in [[Beverly Hills]], California, on December 18, 2017. In the United States, it was set to be released on December 8 and 22, but, two weeks before its debut, it was pushed to December 25 to avoid competition with ''[[Star Wars: The Last Jedi]]''.<ref name="ReleaseDate">{{cite web|last1=Fleming|first1=Mike Jr.|title=Ridley Scott's 'All The Money In The World' Moves To Christmas Day|url=https://deadline.com/2017/12/ridley-scott-getty-kidnap-all-the-money-in-the-world-move-christmas-day-1202221676/|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=December 7, 2017|date=December 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171207084349/http://deadline.com/2017/12/ridley-scott-getty-kidnap-all-the-money-in-the-world-move-christmas-day-1202221676/|archive-date=December 7, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> It was released on digital [[home video]] platforms on March 27, 2018, and on [[DVD]] and [[Blu-ray]] on April 10.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bui |first1=Hoai-Tran |title='All the Money in the World' Exclusive Clip: What It's Like to Work With Ridley Scott |date=March 27, 2018 |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/exclusive-all-the-money-in-the-world-clip/ |publisher=[[/Film]] |access-date=September 8, 2020 |archive-date=August 20, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200820193655/https://www.slashfilm.com/exclusive-all-the-money-in-the-world-clip/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Reception==
===Box office===
''All the Money in the World'' grossed $25.1&nbsp;million in the United States and Canada and $31.8&nbsp;million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $56.9&nbsp;million against a production budget of $50&nbsp;million.<ref name="BOM">{{cite web|url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=allthemoneyintheworld.htm|title=All the Money in the World (2017)|work=[[Box Office Mojo]]|access-date=November 13, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190706112212/https://www.boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=allthemoneyintheworld.htm|archive-date=July 6, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

On Christmas Day, the film's opening day in the United States, it grossed $2.6&nbsp;million from 2,068 theaters.<ref name=opening>{{Cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2017/12/last-jedi-dwayne-johnson-jumanji-zac-efron-greatest-showman-box-office-1202230784/|title='Last Jedi' Now At $99M, 'Jumanji' Huge At $72M+; 'All The Money In The World' Opens To $2.6M – Christmas Weekend|author=Anthony D'Alessandro|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=December 26, 2017|access-date=December 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180223172216/http://deadline.com/2017/12/last-jedi-dwayne-johnson-jumanji-zac-efron-greatest-showman-box-office-1202230784/|archive-date=February 23, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> Its first full weekend, the film made $5.4&nbsp;million from 2,074 theaters, finishing 7th at the box office.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2018/01/last-jedi-jumanji-new-years-weekend-box-office-2018-1202233711/|title='Last Jedi' & 'Jumanji' Duel For No. 1 Over New Year's Weekend As 2017 Box Office Closes With $11.1B – Sunday Update|author=Anthony D'Alessandro|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=December 31, 2017|access-date=December 31, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171231071613/http://deadline.com/2017/12/last-jedi-jumanji-new-years-weekend-box-office-2018-1202233711/|archive-date=December 31, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> The following weekend, the film made $3.6&nbsp;million, a drop of 36%, and finished 10th at the box office.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2018/01/insidious-the-last-key-last-jedi-jumanji-weekend-box-office-1202236009/|title='Jumanji' Goes Wild With $36M; 'Insidious' Rises To $29M+ – Sunday AM B.O. Update|author=Anthony D'Alessandro|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=January 7, 2018|access-date=January 7, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180107174859/http://deadline.com/2018/01/insidious-the-last-key-last-jedi-jumanji-weekend-box-office-1202236009/|archive-date=January 7, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Critical response===
{{Rotten Tomatoes prose|79||260|consensus=''All the Money in the World'' offers an absorbing portrayal of a true story, brought compellingly to life by a powerful performance from Christopher Plummer.|ref=yes|access-date=September 1, 2025}}
[[Metacritic]], which uses a [[Weighted arithmetic mean|weighted average]], assigned the film a score of 72 out of 100, based on 47 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref name="Metacritic">{{cite web |title=''All the Money in the World'' |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/all-the-money-in-the-world |website=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[Fandom (website)#Fandom, Inc.|Fandom, Inc.]] |access-date=September 1, 2025 |archive-url= |archive-date= |url-status=}}</ref> Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "B" on an A+ to F scale.<ref name=opening/>

[[Todd McCarthy]] of ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' called the film "a terrifically dexterous and detailed thriller about the Italian mob's 1973 kidnapping for ransom of the grandson of the world's richest man, John Paul Getty [sic]."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/review/all-the-money-in-the-world-1069161|title='All the Money in the World': Film Review|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=December 19, 2017 |publisher=[[Prometheus Global Media|Prometheus Global Media, LLC]]|access-date=December 19, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171221045142/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/review/all-the-money-in-the-world-1069161|archive-date=December 21, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Matt Zoller Seitz]] of ''[[RogerEbert.com]]'' gave the film three out of four stars and commended it as a whole, but criticized the middle section as repetitive. He also praised Scott for being able to finish the film despite the Spacey controversy, calling it "a testament to the awesome work ethic of its 80-year old but still apparently tireless director".<ref>{{cite web|last1=Seitz|first1=Matt Zoller|author-link1=Matt Zoller Seitz|title=All the Money in the World Movie Review (2017)|url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/all-the-money-in-the-world-2017|website=[[RogerEbert.com]]|publisher=Ebert Digital LLC|access-date=December 25, 2017|date=December 23, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171225035158/https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/all-the-money-in-the-world-2017|archive-date=December 25, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Peter Bradshaw]] of ''[[The Guardian]]'' gave the film four out of five stars, reserving his greatest praise for Plummer, who, he said, "doesn’t look like a hasty replacement. He relishes and luxuriates in the role. It fits him perfectly."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2017/dec/19/all-the-money-in-the-world-review-getty-kevin-spacey-christopher-plummer-ridley-scott|title=All the Money in the World review – raucous crime thriller banishes ghost of Kevin Spacey|first=Peter|last=Bradshaw|date=December 19, 2017|website=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=January 29, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180129003156/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2017/dec/19/all-the-money-in-the-world-review-getty-kevin-spacey-christopher-plummer-ridley-scott|archive-date=January 29, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> Writing for ''[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]]'', [[David Edelstein]] praised "the marvelous performance of Michelle Williams as Gail. It's a real transformation."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vulture.com/2017/12/all-the-money-in-the-world-movie-review.html|title=Christopher Plummer Is Getting Headlines for ''All the Money in the World'', But It's Michelle Williams Who Deserves Them|date=December 20, 2017|first=David|last=Edelstein|website=[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181103090646/http://www.vulture.com/2017/12/all-the-money-in-the-world-movie-review.html|archive-date=November 3, 2018|url-status=live|access-date=April 20, 2021}}</ref>
